decision: Every pull request must be validated against the knowledge graph rules, with findings posted as an advisory comment and never as a merge block.
why: Without automated validation, rule violations reach the codebase unchallenged and the graph stops describing what the code actually does.
steps: On pull_request opened, synchronize, or reopened, check out the repo at the PR head with full history.
Collect the full diff (git diff origin/<base>...HEAD) and the full content of every non-deleted changed file. Cap total injected content at 50 KB; truncate with a note beyond that.

Run claude -p with the diff and file contents from the repo root so CLAUDE.md context loads automatically. Ask Claude to return JSON: {"result": "PASS" | "FAIL", "violations": [{"rule": "<id>", "violation": "<matched violation text>", "evidence": "<file and content>"}]}.
Parse the JSON output. If result is FAIL, format each violation as a bullet citing the rule id, the violation text, and the evidence.
Post the formatted findings as a pull request comment. If result is PASS, post a single passing confirmation.
Exit 0 regardless of result — this check is advisory and must not block merge.
violations: Workflow authenticating with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead of CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
Validation configured as a required status check, blocking merge on findings.
Claude invoked outside the repo root, losing CLAUDE.md context and the knowledge graph.
